(a) Members Eligible to Request Review of Retirement or Separation Without Pay for Physical Disability.—Section 1554(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) by striking “an officer” and inserting “a member or former member of the uniformed services”; and 
        (2) by striking “his case” and inserting “the member’s case”.  
    (b) Limitation on Reduction in Personnel Assigned to Duty With Service Review Agency.—1559(a) of such title is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that letting members or former members request review of a disability separation grants a right to formally object to a federal decision. But this only widens who may seek an individual personnel review of their own case before a military review board, which is closer to an internal appeal than outside consultation on a federal policy decision. The second amendment simply extends a date limiting personnel reductions at the service review agency. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or new right to sue.
fable.s: by striking “an officer” and inserting “a member or former member of the uniformed services”

qwen_block.w: This section amends existing statutes to broaden the class of individuals eligible to request a review of their retirement or separation status and to extend a deadline for personnel reductions. It does not establish a new process for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards involving non-federal members. The 'review' mentioned is an administrative appeal process for service members, which falls under internal government procedures or individual rights to appeal, not the definition of participation involving outside parties in decision-making.
qwen_block.s: (a) Members Eligible to Request Review of Retirement or Separation Without Pay for Physical Disability.—Section 1554(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “an officer” and inserting “a member or former member of the uniformed services”; and (2) by striking “his case” and inserting “the member’s case”. (b) Limitation on Reduction in Personnel Assigned to Duty With Service Review Agency.—1559(a) of such title is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.

opus.w: This amendment widens who can ask for review of their own disability retirement or separation. That is an individual appeal of a personnel decision, not participation by outsiders in a federal policy decision. Subsection (b) only changes a date limiting reductions in staff at a federal agency, which stays inside the government. The 'right to object' reading is tempting, but this is the same kind of case-specific appeal as in Example 11.
opus.s: by striking “an officer” and inserting “a member or former member of the uniformed services”
opus.b: The tempting reading is that letting a member or former member ask a board to review their disability retirement or separation counts as a "formal objection" to a federal decision. That reading fails because the review concerns only that person's own case. It works like an appeal of an individual determination (as in Example 11), not outside input into a policy decision. Subsection (b) only extends a date limiting staff cuts at a federal agency, which is purely internal.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends eligibility criteria for requesting a review of retirement or separation and adjusts personnel limits for a review agency. It does not establish a process for public consultation, advisory committees with outside members, or public comment periods. The ability to request a review of one's own personnel action is an administrative remedy, not the type of public participation defined in the instructions (which focuses on outside parties influencing federal decisions through consultation, hearings, or advisory roles).
qwen_chat.s: (a) Members Eligible to Request Review of Retirement or Separation Without Pay for Physical Disability.—Section 1554(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “an officer” and inserting “a member or former member of the uniformed services”; and (2) by striking “his case” and inserting “the member’s case”. (b) Limitation on Reduction in Personnel Assigned to Duty With Service Review Agency.—1559(a) of such title is amended by striking “December 31, 2010” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allowing a "member or former member" to request a review involves participation because it gives an individual a voice in a government decision. However, this is an administrative appeal process regarding an individual's specific benefit or status (retirement/separation), not a mechanism for public input into general policy or regulatory decisions. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, and this is functionally similar to an appeal of a personnel action. Furthermore, the text itself is merely amending statutory language regarding eligibility and personnel limits, not establishing a new participatory process.
